fixed.how: folderHold(git, branch, base) holds the rebuild (held: 'commits') whenever the task's branch or the folder's HEAD has a commit that GitHub's branch lacks. Forerunner's own unpushed states are exempt: the base-merge shape and WIP commits. Any commit it cannot identify holds the rebuild, so it fails closed. If Forerunner's own rebuild never reached GitHub, it is put back: immediately when the push fails (putBack), or at the next try after a crash (REBUILD_PENDING_REF / REBUILD_BEFORE_*). The poll writes the wait on the record (DependentBranches.sayFolderWait, last_outcome owed_folder_commits). A plain wait gets its words back once the folder is clean (folderWaitOver).

fixed.how: Root cause: settleRecord (session/dependent-branches.ts) compared ownBefore with ownAfter. Both were read from GitHub's branch, which already held the pushed commit, and neither was compared with the record. The fix adds reviewedChangeBefore: the branch's own change before the rebuild must equal the record's own_change_id, the same rule ReviewedPrMerge.keepsOwnChange uses. With no own_change_id, the head must equal reviewed_head_sha. A rebuild whose push failed had already moved the record to its own head and change, so it still rebuilds. When the change differs, changedAfterReview runs. It leaves the record at the reviewed commit as left_to_you with head_moved and headMovedSentence ('#N changed after the review: look at the new commits, then merge it yourself or redo the task.'), so there is no Merge. It sets approval to none, which drops a kept press. One card says it: an open merge card takes the words, and a new card is filed only when the record was not already waiting for the person, as the merge step's settle does. Said once.
